A study published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2021 (Issue 5, CD001150) highlights the use of sunflower seed oil applied topically to prevent invasive bacterial infections in preterm infants in Egypt. This was demonstrated through a randomized, controlled clinical trial (Pediatr Infect Dis J, 2004; 23(8):719-25). 2. Fraser et al. discussed the respiratory complications associated with preterm birth in their article published in BMJ (2004; 329(7472):962-5). 3. Stoll et al. analyzed trends in care practices, morbidity, and mortality among extremely preterm neonates from 1993 to 2012, as published in JAMA (2015; 314(10):1039-51). 4. Sweet et al. provided updated European consensus guidelines on managing respiratory distress syndrome in neonates in 2019 (Neonatology, 2019; 115(4):432-50). 5. Gregory et al.1333-40). 6. Soll and Barkhuff reviewed the role of noninvasive ventilation in the era of surfactant administration in Clin Perinatol (2019; 46(3):493-516). 7. Ho et al. examined the use of CPAP for respiratory distress in preterm infants in a systematic review (Cochrane Database Syst Rev, 2020; Issue 10, CD002271). They also compared early versus delayed CPAP initiation in another review (Cochrane Database Syst Rev, 2020; Issue 10, CD002975). 8. The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued recommendations for the care of preterm or low-birth-weight infants, emphasizing interventions such as kangaroo mother care, thermal care, feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and the use of emollients. 9. For those requiring ventilation, the cord should be clamped to allow effective ventilation. 10. Surfactant replacement therapy is recommended for intubated and ventilated newborns with respiratory distress syndrome. Early administration (within the first two hours after birth) is preferred over delayed rescue therapy. 11. Oxygen therapy for preterm infants born at or before 32 weeks of gestation should begin with 30% oxygen or air, rather than 100% oxygen. Higher oxygen concentrations should only be used if the heart rate remains below 60 beats per minute after 30 seconds of adequate ventilation. 12. Family-centered care, including parental involvement, education, counseling, and peer support, is emphasized in neonatal care guidelines. This approach has been shown to improve parental satisfaction and reduce readmission rates for preterm infants. 13. Studies have highlighted the importance of family involvement in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) and during the transition from NICU to home. Interventions such as home visits and discharge preparation are critical for improving outcomes for preterm infants and their families. 14. The WHO and other organizations continue to develop and update guidelines to improve neonatal care, including recommendations for resuscitation, infection prevention, and developmental care. 15. Research has also explored the use of bubble CPAP in low-resource settings, identifying barriers and facilitators to its implementation. Studies from sub-Saharan Africa and other regions have provided insights into the challenges and successes of introducing this technology. 16. Caffeine therapy has been extensively studied for the treatment of apnea of prematurity. It has been shown to reduce the incidence of intermittent hypoxemia and improve long-term outcomes in preterm infants. 17. Family-centered care interventions, including parental leave policies and peer support, have been shown to enhance the well-being of families and improve neonatal outcomes. These approaches are particularly important in lowand middle-income countries. 18. The WHO emphasizes the importance of systems thinking and community-based primary health care to strengthen maternal, neonatal, and child health services globally. 19. Postpartum depression is a significant concern among mothers of preterm and low-birth-weight infants. Systematic reviews have identified risk factors and highlighted the need for targeted interventions to support maternal mental health. 20. Qualitative studies have explored the experiences of caregivers and health workers in providing care for preterm and low-birth-weight infants, particularly in rural and low-resource settings. These insights inform strategies to improve neonatal care delivery and caregiver engagement. This content reflects a comprehensive overview of neonatal care practices, research findings, and global health recommendations aimed at improving outcomes for preterm and low-birth-weight infants.
